chips.memory: 192 GiB HBM per chip; 7,380 GB/s HBM bandwidth; 1,200 GB/s bidirectional inter-chip bandwidth.
chips.die: Google describes two chiplets per logical chip but does not publish bare-die dimensions in the cited document.
chips.bench: No independent workload benchmark imported. Cloud topology, compiler, model, and framework materially affect results.
chips.headline: Google's current cloud TPU baseline, with chiplet topology and HBM bandwidth visible instead of hidden behind a pod score.
chips.caveat: TPU7x is exposed as two devices per chip in the programming model. HBM and interconnect figures are not directly comparable with client GPU memory metrics.

chips.name: AWS Trainium3
chips.launch: AWS documents Trainium3 as its fourth-generation Trainium accelerator family.
chips.process: Foundry and process node are not specified on the cited AWS product page.
chips.cpu: AI accelerator, not a host CPU.
chips.gpu: Trainium3 NeuronCore compute engine with eight large cores and dedicated tensor, vector, scalar, and GPSIMD engines.
chips.ai: AWS claims up to 2× MXFP8 compute throughput versus Trainium2. A comparable generic TOPS figure is not imported.
chips.memory: 144 GB HBM3e per chip and 4.9 TB/s bandwidth. AWS also describes hardware W4A8 quantization and a two-level on-chip SRAM hierarchy.
chips.die: No verified bare-die dimensions or licensed die photograph imported.
chips.bench: No independent application benchmark imported. AWS throughput claims depend on precision, model, software, and system configuration.
chips.headline: A hyperscaler accelerator baseline with memory and compute-engine structure documented separately from marketing throughput.
chips.caveat: The 2× figure is a vendor generation-over-generation claim, not a normalized cross-accelerator score. HBM bandwidth is reported in decimal TB/s on the AWS page.

chips.name: SiFive Performance P870-D
chips.launch: SiFive presents P870-D as a licensable RISC-V processor for datacenter workloads.
chips.process: Process node is application-dependent and not specified on the cited product page.
chips.cpu: 64-bit, six-wide, out-of-order RISC-V core with RVA23 compliance; up to 64 clusters and up to 256 coherent cores through cluster and chiplet configurations.
chips.gpu: CPU IP, not a graphics processor.

chips.memory: Cluster-cache and coherent-fabric details are documented, but no platform memory bandwidth is asserted for a finished SoC.
chips.die: P870-D is licensable processor IP; no single physical die footprint exists to import.
chips.bench: SiFive quotes >2 SpecInt2K17/GHz as a product-page target. It is a vendor claim and not entered as a benchmark score.
chips.headline: A current datacenter-oriented RISC-V baseline that keeps licensable core IP distinct from a fabricated chip.
chips.caveat: P870-D configurations depend on the licensee's SoC or chiplet implementation. Core count and quoted integer targets do not establish a finished product's performance.

chips.name: NVIDIA Rubin GPU
